newsitem.title: ITALY: Eight climbers killed in Italian Alps.
newsitem.headline: Eight climbers killed in Italian Alps.

text.p: Eight climbers died and the wife of a senior German diplomat was missing after a series of accidents in the Italian Alps, police said on Tuesday.
Four men were killed when they fell more than 100 metres (330 feet) from the approach to the 3,850-metre (12,631-foot) summit of the Great Zebru mountain near the Swiss and Austrian borders.

Another three climbers died in a separate incident on the same mountain later in the day. One of them was a 44-year-old Alpine guide who had witnessed the first accident and alerted mountain rescue services.
"It's very difficult to say what caused these accidents," Lorenzo Zampeti, head of the Bolzano mountain rescue service, told Italian national television.
"But mountaineering is an intrinsically dangerous sport. It's not like taking a walk in a square in Milan or Rome."
Fifty miles (80 km) further east, a 62-year-old man, part of a five-strong expedition, died after falling 50 metres (165 feet) from Mount Pelmo near Belluno. His companions were all safe.
Police in Bolzano also mounted a search for Anna Maria Neuner, 56, wife of a top German diplomat at the Vatican, who failed to return from a hike.
She was last seen at 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Monday near a mountain refuge where she had been lodging.
There has been a rash of mountaineering deaths in the Italian Alps this summer.
Five people were killed on Europe's highest peak, Mont Blanc, at the weekend, bringing the number of deaths on the Italian face of that mountain alone to 27 in the past three weeks.
The last notable accidents on Great Zebru were in 1994, when three German climbers died, and in 1989 when four Italians were killed.
